Devour

/dih-VOR/ — stress on second syllable, rhymes with 'for' · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To devour something is to eat or take it in eagerly and completely, often very quickly.

The hikers devoured the entire pot of stew in minutes.

Worked Example

At the pizza party, the teenagers devoured three large pizzas in under twenty minutes, eating with enthusiasm and speed.

Devour is more precise than 'eat' because it carries the sense of eager and complete consumption, plus speed. 'Eat' is neutral; 'devour' shows both enthusiasm and totality, making it ideal when speed and eagerness matter.

How Devour Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

eat

eat: take in food in the ordinary way

consume

consume: use up or take in completely

gobble

gobble: eat hastily in large mouthfuls

Antonyms

savor

savor: taste slowly in order to enjoy fully

nibble

nibble: take small, careful bites at a time

How Strong Is It? — nibble → eat → gorge → devour

nibble vs. devour

nibble vs. devour: Nibble is far weaker than devour; nibble takes tiny, careful bites, while devour eats everything up eagerly and fast.

eat vs. devour

eat vs. devour: Eat is neutral and weaker than devour; eat simply takes in food, while devour does so greedily and completely.

gorge vs. devour

gorge vs. devour: Gorge is close to devour, but devour stresses eager, rapid consumption, while gorge stresses stuffing oneself to painful excess.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — de-

Prefix — de-: down; completely (intensive) (Latin)

Root — vour

Root — vour: to swallow, eat (from Latin vorare, 'to swallow')

Put it together

Put it together: De- ('completely') + vour ('to swallow,' from Latin vorare): to devour is to swallow something down completely — to eat it up eagerly and fast.

Use the root in a new word: voracious

Use the root in a new word: voracious: A voracious reader devours one book after another; both words share a root meaning 'to swallow.'

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral / colloquial

Devour works when someone eats eagerly, completely, and quickly—showing real enthusiasm. It's less formal than 'consume' and more emphatic than 'eat'. Use it when the speed and eagerness matter to your meaning.
